Heatmap of a cluster solution

Source: R/seg_cluster.R
seg_plot_heatmap.Rd

Plots the prepared clustering variables of a random sample of respondents as a heatmap with dendrograms, built with ggplot2:

Usage

seg_plot_heatmap(
  object,
  n = 200,
  row_order = c("cluster", "dendrogram"),
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

object

A seg_cluster object, e.g. from seg_cluster().

n

Number of respondents sampled (proportionally to the cluster sizes, at least 2 per cluster). Defaults to 200. NULL uses all respondents.

row_order

How to order the respondents: "cluster" (default) or "dendrogram", see "Details".

seed

Random seed for the sample. The global random seed is left untouched. Defaults to 123.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

  • Cells: the values of the prepared clustering variables (e.g. z-standardized), from low (blue) to high (red). Extreme values are capped at the 1st and 99th percentile, so that a few outliers do not dominate the colors.

  • Top dendrogram: hierarchical clustering of the variables (Ward's method), so that variables with similar answer patterns are next to each other.

  • Left dendrogram and color bar: the respondents and their cluster.

With row_order = "cluster" (default), respondents are grouped by cluster; within each cluster, they are ordered by a hierarchical clustering, whose dendrogram is drawn in the color of the cluster. Clear blocks of color within a cluster indicate a homogeneous cluster with a distinct profile.

With row_order = "dendrogram", the respondents are ordered by a hierarchical clustering of the whole sample (Ward's method), as in a classical heatmap, independently of the cluster solution. The color bar then shows whether the clusters of the solution correspond to the structure found by the hierarchical clustering; branches containing respondents of a single cluster are drawn in its color.

See also

Other clustering: predict.seg_cluster(), seg_agreement(), seg_as_cluster(), seg_cluster(), seg_cluster_density(), seg_cluster_fuzzy(), seg_cluster_hierarchical(), seg_cluster_hkmeans(), seg_cluster_model(), seg_cluster_partitioning(), seg_dbscan_eps(), seg_plot_centers(), seg_plot_cluster(), seg_plot_dend()

Examples

# \donttest{
prep <- seg_prep_data(
  sm_synthetic,
  vars = dplyr::starts_with("F50_0_"),
  missing = "mice",
  max_missing_prop = 0.2,
  verbose = FALSE
)
cl <- seg_cluster(prep, k = 4, plots = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
seg_plot_heatmap(cl)

seg_plot_heatmap(cl, n = 300, row_order = "dendrogram")

# }
